---
title: "Revision-pinned CUDA parameter transfer"
---

`Cellerator::framework_parameter_transfer` bridges the native conditional
`ParameterStore` and CUDA runtime. It transfers the exact caller-selected
`ExpertKey` using an immutable `ParameterLease`; a newer published revision or a
cache miss cannot substitute another payload. The public header is
`Cellerator/modeling/cuda/parameter_transfer.hh`.

`ParameterTransfer::upload(store, key, stream)` acquires that exact revision,
copies its execution-parameter bytes into an owned `PinnedBuffer`, enqueues a
real `cudaMemcpyAsync` H2D through `DeviceBuffer`, and records an `Event` on the
supplied stream. It also accepts a lease from `ParameterStore::snapshot`.
Source buffers must explicitly name `device="host"`. Storage types are opaque:
FP16, FP32 and packed bytes are copied unchanged, without numerical conversion.
This bridge does not transfer master parameters, gradients or optimizer state.

The copyable transfer ticket owns the source revision, staging allocation,
device buffer and readiness event. `ready()` queries transfer completion;
`wait()` waits for it. `view()` returns a borrowed immutable device view only
after upload completion. The last owner drains upload before releasing its
resources. Host copying and allocations happen synchronously during submission;
only the staged H2D copy is asynchronously enqueued.

For asynchronous downstream use, acquire a separate execution lease:

```cpp
auto transfer = ParameterTransfer::upload(store, selected_key, upload_stream);
auto execution = transfer.acquire_on(compute_stream);
auto parameters = execution.view();
// Launch consumers of parameters on compute_stream.
execution.finish();  // Record completion after every consumer was enqueued.
// Poll execution.ready(), or execution.wait().
```

`acquire_on` inserts a device-side stream wait for upload and retains the
transfer's entire ownership. Destroying the transfer ticket therefore cannot
invalidate an active execution lease. `finish()` seals the lease and records a
completion event; view access after sealing is rejected. Multiple streams may
hold independent execution leases for the same immutable transfer. The caller
must retain each borrowed stream until `finish()` records its event and must not
enqueue additional consumers after sealing. Backward that reads parameters needs
its own retained execution lease or must precede the existing lease's finish.

Lease destruction waits for its completion event, or drains the consumer stream
if `finish()` was omitted, before releasing parameter storage. Explicit `wait()`
surfaces CUDA errors. A destructor that cannot establish completion terminates
rather than release potentially active storage; destructors may block and are
not a nonblocking reclamation service. An exception between copy enqueue and
event recording also drains the stream before resources unwind.

`required_memory(lease)` validates the source and reports memory without CUDA
calls. New allocations are one execution-parameter-sized pinned host buffer and
one equally sized device buffer. The source revision remains retained, including
its master/gradient/optimizer buffers; `retained_source_bytes` conservatively
sums all declared buffer lengths, counting aliases separately. Existing source
bytes are retained, not newly allocated. Staging remains owned until the last
transfer/execution lease is destroyed. Account these explicit costs when using
the [native placement planner](native_scheduling.qmd); this bridge does not reserve
a budget, discover devices, evict a cache or perform multi-GPU/network movement.

The [smoke source](../tests/framework/cuda/parameter_transfer_smoke.cu) has a
`--host-only` path for exact-revision retention, byte accounting, missing-source
and non-host rejection without CUDA calls. Its GPU path independently compares
downloaded bytes, destroys an upload ticket before consumer completion, publishes
and retires a revision while executing, and checks the fallback destruction
drain. This change was compiled for SM70 and host contracts were run; the GPU path
was not executed and performance is unmeasured.
